judge_assessment.explanation: Every claim checks out against the artifacts. Problems 1, 4, 9 and 10 ask for an expanded form, but verify.json ids 1, 4, 9 and 10 are `eval` identities whose `expected` is the number the stem already gives (546, 907, 470, 375) - the decomposition sits in the `at` givens, so the check only confirms the addends sum to the target and never checks the form the child writes; 500 + 46 would satisfy id 1 exactly as 500 + 40 + 6 does. Problem 10 is worse than the judge states: the stem asks for the new number in standard AND expanded form, and the single check is 300+60+5+10 = 375, which is the start-plus-ten arithmetic, not either requested form. Problem 6 asks for two standard-form rewrites and then the symbol; id 6 is one `compare` relation. Problem 7 prints 'Explain what Maya did wrong' plus the correction, and id 7 is a bare `eval` for 615 - the sheet's only manual entry is 9(a), the number name. The quick-answer bank does print 546, 907, 470 and 375 as the answers to problems that asked for expanded forms. The fourth page carries problem 10 alone. Two findings the judge did not report: the bank prints '—' for problem 6, so a verified relation answer is delivered as no answer at all, and that is a reproducible renderer bug, not a one-off.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7's misconception is encoded as a declared, machine-proved trap (6015 from writing the digit 6 and then the two digits of 'fifteen' side by side) and the key turns it into a remediation the grader can act on - 'have them build the number with base-ten blocks: 6 flats, 1 rod, 5 units'. Keep the trap-to-grading-note pipeline.

The zero-place thread is carried through all three documents deliberately: worksheet problem 4 (907) and problem 5 (600 + 5), key solution 5 ('otherwise the 5 would slide over into the tens place and make 65'), and the study guide's closing watch-out box naming both 907 and 605. That is the single largest error source at this grade and it is taught, practised and graded consistently.

Problem 8 (order 700 + 8, seven hundred eighty, 78) is a genuinely well-built compare-across-forms item: three different representations, a two-digit distractor, and a `compare` check with "order": "asc" whose expected [78, 708, 780] is printed correctly in the bank.

root_causes.description: The coverage gate is defined per problem id, not per printed response. verify.py fails only when some id in 1..problem_count has no entry at all, so a problem that prints several required responses is fully satisfied by one scalar check, and both the gate log and the delivery message then describe the sheet as completely verified.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 9 prints an inline 'Word form: \underline{\hspace{9cm}}' line inside the stem plus \problem's automatic answer blank - two slots - and verify.json gives it one eval (470) plus one manual (the number name).
worksheet.tex problem 6 asks for two standard-form rewrites and a symbol; verify.json id 6 is a single compare entry.
worksheet.tex problem 10 asks for standard form and expanded form; verify.json id 10 is a single eval whose expected is 375.
scripts/verify.py's coverage gate only reports 'Coverage gap' for an id with no entries at all, so all of the above pass.

root_causes.description: There is no check type that can verify a place-value representation, so the author fell back on identity-style eval checks whose expected value is the standard form. That is why the requested expanded forms are unverifiable in principle here, and why the quick-answer bank had nothing but the standard form to print.
evidence: verify.json ids 1, 4, 9, 10 all use "type": "eval" with the standard form as `expected` for problems whose printed task is 'write ... in expanded form'.
SKILL.md's type table has no representation/form check; the closest types (eval, equiv, compare) all compare values, not written forms.

final_response.md defends the encoding - 'each expanded form is evaluated and compared against the standard form it must equal, with the place values lifted into named givens so the checker sees them' - which is exactly the identity check the judge flagged.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to reframe error-analysis items 'via the ordinary types' and, a few lines later, to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Nothing states that an item doing both needs both entries, and no gate enforces it, so the explanation slot is dropped and the sheet reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7: 'Explain what Maya did wrong, then write the correct standard form.' verify.json id 7 is a single eval with a trap and no manual entry.

verify.json contains exactly one manual entry (id 9, the number name), so the answer key's manual-review note appears only on problem 9 while problem 7's explanation is silently counted as machine-verified.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expected values and falls back to the em-dash on failure, so relation answers ('<', '>', '=') from compare checks can never appear in the Quick Answers bank.
evidence: verify.json id 6 has "expected": "<" and the compiled answer_key.pdf Quick Answers block prints '6. —'.
Running scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt on '<', '>' and '=' returns '---' in all three cases because sympy.sympify raises on the token.

root_causes.description: The page budget accepts any compiled length inside a wide range, so a sheet can spill one short problem onto a nearly empty final page without any gate noticing.
evidence: gate_log.txt: 'Page budget (ws, letter): 10 problems, 59.0cm of content / ideal 3 page(s) - accepted range 2-5' and then '4 page(s), within the 5-page budget'.
worksheet.pdf page 4 contains only problem 10 (a two-line stem plus a 6cm workspace), leaving most of the sheet blank.

improvements.title: Make verification coverage per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py's coverage gate currently passes as soon as every id in 1..problem_count carries one entry (scripts/verify.py, the `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]` check). Replace that with a slot-level contract: add a build gate that counts the response slots a problem actually prints (each \ansline/\answerline/\ansblank, each \underline{} write-on rule in a stem, each lettered part (a)/(b)/(c), each row of a fill-in table or partially blank sequence) and fails the build unless that id declares at least as many verify entries. Add the matching rule to SKILL.md's JSON-format paragraph, which today only says 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'. For this case the rule bites on problems 6, 9 and 10, each of which prints two required responses and declares one check.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_answer_slots.py plus a fixture pair under tests/fixtures/: a worksheet .tex whose problem 1 prints two response slots (an inline \underline{} line inside the stem and \problem's automatic answer blank) and a verify.json carrying a single scalar entry for id 1. The gate must exit 1 naming 'problem 1 prints 2 response slots but declares 1 check'. Today build.sh runs that fixture green, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the dominant hard-failure class in this shard: a worksheet can no longer print several required responses per problem while reporting itself fully verified.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is a heuristic over LaTeX and prose, so it will over-count on stems that use \underline for emphasis. Keep it a fail-with-named-slot gate (never a silent skip) and allow an explicit per-problem "slots" override in the verify JSON so a genuine one-slot problem can declare that rather than being blocked.

improvements.title: Add a place-value form check type so expanded and word forms are verifiable
improvements.proposed_change: Add a `place_value_form` check to scripts/verify.py: given "number": 546 and "form": "expanded" with "expected": "500 + 40 + 6", decompose the number into its non-zero place-value addends and require the expected string to be exactly that ordered list of terms - so 500 + 46 and 90 + 7 fail while 900 + 7 passes. Support "form": "word" by generating the English number name (hyphen and no-'and' conventions are deterministic below 1,000) and comparing case-insensitively, which also retires the manual entry currently needed for problem 9(a). Because the bank renders `expected`, the Quick Answers column then prints 500 + 40 + 6 instead of 546, which fixes the second hard failure at the same time. Document the type in SKILL.md's type table and in references/problem-library.md's reframing section.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_branches.py add place_value_form cases: 546/expanded with '500 + 40 + 6' PASSES, 546/expanded with '500 + 46' FAILS, 907/expanded with '90 + 7' FAILS while '900 + 7' PASSES, and 470/word with 'four hundred seventy' PASSES while 'four hundred and seventy' FAILS. Every case errors out today because the type does not exist (strict schema, exit 1).
improvements.expected_impact: The requested representation becomes the checked object across the whole elementary place-value band, and the answer bank stops reprinting the number the problem handed the student.
improvements.risk: Word-form generation has convention edge cases (hyphenation of forty-six, no 'and' in US usage). Cap the type at whole numbers below 1,000,000 and return MANUAL rather than FAIL outside that range so the gate never asserts a convention it cannot defend.

improvements.title: Require a paired manual entry for every explain / name-the-error / mark-it response
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md carries two rules that pull in opposite directions: the reframing paragraph says error analysis should be encoded 'via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right', while the paragraph eight lines later says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Authors resolve that by encoding only the numeric correction and dropping the explanation slot. Rewrite the reframing paragraph to state the pairing explicitly: an error-analysis or model-completion item that ALSO prints an explain / name-the-error / circle / cross-out / draw / label slot needs BOTH the typed check for the correction AND a manual entry for that slot under the same id (the curr-088 and curr-100 verify files in this same shard are the worked pattern). Back it with the slot gate so the rule is mechanical, not advisory. In this case problem 7's 'Explain what Maya did wrong' is the slot that vanished.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_answer_slots.py with a fixture whose problem stem contains an imperative open-response verb ('Explain in one sentence', 'Circle', 'Draw', 'Label', 'Cross out', 'Which measurement did ... actually find?') and whose verify.json entry for that id is a bare eval. The gate must exit 1 demanding a paired {"type": "manual"} entry. The same fixture passes once the manual entry is added. Today it passes in both states, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The build's manual-item count becomes trustworthy: exit 2 and the 'flagged manual-review items' banner appear whenever a sheet asks a child to explain, mark or draw something, instead of the build reporting all-green on unreviewed reasoning.
improvements.risk: More sheets exit 2 rather than 0, which looks like a regression on dashboards that treat exit 0 as success. That is the intended trust signal; document it in the build-driver section of SKILL.md so exit 2 is not read as a failure.

improvements.title: Quick Answers must print the form the problem asked for
improvements.proposed_change: The bank renders each id's `expected` values, so when `expected` is the standard form of a number the problem told the student to expand, the bank hands the grader the question rather than the answer (this sheet prints 546, 907, 470 and 375 for four expanded-form problems). Once `place_value_form` lands, make the bank prefer a form-typed entry over a value-typed one for the same id, and add a build-time lint that fails when a problem stem contains 'in expanded form' / 'in word form' / 'in factored form' while the id's rendered bank text is the bare value named in the stem.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py assert that for a stem reading 'Write 546 in expanded form' with a place_value_form entry the bank line is '1. $500 + 40 + 6$', and that a verify file pairing that stem with a bare eval whose expected is 546 fails the new lint. Both assertions fail against today's renderer.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader scanning the bank can mark the sheet without opening the worked solutions, which is the bank's entire purpose.
improvements.risk: The stem lint is text matching and could fire on a stem that quotes the phrase 'expanded form' in passing; make it a named failure with the offending stem quoted so it is one keystroke to see whether it is real.

improvements.title: Render compare/relation answers in the Quick Answers bank instead of an em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt sends every string `expected` through sympy.sympify and falls back to '---' on SympifyError. The relation answers a `compare` check with "order": "relation" produces ("<", ">", "=") never parse, so a fully verified relation always prints as '---' - the same glyph the bank uses for a manual-only id, which tells a grader 'see solution' when the verified answer is known. Special-case the three relation tokens before the sympify attempt and emit $<$, $>$, $=$; for an id whose entries mix a relation with values, join them (e.g. '439 $<$ 493'). Problem 6 of this worksheet is the live example: a verified '<' delivered as '6. —'.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py add a verify fixture containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["400+30+9", "493"], "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} and assert the generated bank line for id 1 contains '$<$' and not '---'. It fails today (_fmt('<') returns '---') and passes after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Every comparison problem - a whole facet in the grade 2-3 place-value and fraction topics - gets a real at-a-glance answer instead of a blank, and the em-dash goes back to meaning only 'manual'.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper; the '---' fallback stays for genuinely unrenderable values.

improvements.title: Warn when the last worksheet page is nearly empty
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/page_budget.py already computes an ideal page count and an accepted range; have the compile step compare the ideal against the compiled count and, when the compiled sheet exceeds the ideal and the final page holds a single problem, emit an exit-2 layout warning naming the problem and suggesting the workspace reduction or reflow that would close the gap. This sheet compiled to 4 pages against an ideal of 3, with problem 10 alone on page 4.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_page_budget.py add a fixture whose content measures to an ideal of 3 pages but compiles to 4 with one problem on the last page; assert the warning fires and names that problem. No warning is produced today.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the recurring 'one short item and substantial unused space' finding that cost this case two points on visual and print quality.
improvements.risk: A warning only, never a build failure - a challenge problem deliberately given its own page is legitimate and the author must stay free to keep it.

case_summary: The mathematics, the worked solutions and the study guide on this sheet are all sound - independent conversion of all ten problems agrees with the key, and the zero-place misconception is taught and graded coherently across the three documents. The rejection is entirely about what the verifier actually checks. Four problems ask for an expanded form and are verified by an identity whose expected value is the number the problem handed the student; the quick-answer bank then prints those same numbers as the answers. Problem 6 asks for two rewrites and a symbol and receives one relation check whose answer the bank drops entirely as an em-dash. Problem 7 asks for an explanation and is recorded as machine-verified. The fix is not more care but three mechanical changes: a slot-level coverage gate, a check type that can verify a written place-value form, and a renderer that can print a relation.
